commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Disagg] Allow MoRIIO HMA per-layer block_len
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

MoRIIO KV cache registration under HMA requires a uniform `block_len` across attention layers. Hybrid models (GLM-5.2 DSA, MiniMax, Gemma4) register layers with different per-layer `block_len` / `block_size` (e.g. `9216` vs page default `2112`). Registration then raises:

```
ValueError: MoRIIO KV cache block length mismatch for layer ...: 9216 != 2112
```

and PD bring-up fails at health-gate. Layer transfers already size RDMA from per-layer geometry; the uniform check is stricter than the transfer path.

## Changes

`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py` (KV registration):

- Allow divergent per-layer `block_len` (bytes) always; log at debug per layer; advertise `max(block_lens)` to the peer with a single summary `logger.info`.
- Allow divergent `block_size` (tokens/page) **only when hybrid KV cache manager (HMA) is enabled** (Gemma4 SWA/full-attn from #53721). Without HMA, still raise on any `block_size` mismatch (including when `block_len` also differs — ChuanLi's case).
- Per-layer spam logs moved to `logger.debug` (okorzh).

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py`:

- divergent `block_len` allowed
- divergent `block_size` rejected without HMA
- size+len both differ still rejected without HMA
- divergent `block_size` allowed with HMA (Gemma4)

## Test Plan

### Unit

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py -k 'register_kv_caches_allows_hybrid or register_kv_caches_rejects_divergent or register_kv_caches_allows_hma' -q
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Register int8 scaled_mm as a custom op
commits.pr_body:
### What is wrong

`TritonInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel.apply_weights` calls `triton_scaled_mm` directly at line 134. That function is plain Python. It picks a tile shape from `triton.next_power_of_2(M)`, does some reshapes and asserts, then launches a Triton kernel.

There is no custom op wrapper around it, so dynamo and inductor trace straight into all of that. The fp8 block scaled path a few lines below in the same file does have one, registered as `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm_func`. So fp8 is opaque to the compiler and int8 is not.

### What it costs

Measured on gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S, Strix Halo), vLLM 0.28.0 built for ROCm 7.2. One linear layer at the fused gate_up shape N=34816 K=5120, one token of decode so M=1:

```
eager, called directly              1.321 ms    134.9 GB/s
torch.compile, called directly     38.072 ms      4.7 GB/s
torch.compile, through a custom op  1.314 ms    135.6 GB/s
```

End to end on a Qwen3.5 27B model quantized to int8 w8a8 with AMD Quark. Same server flags both runs, default cudagraph mode, the patch is the only difference:

```
                  single stream    4 concurrent
before             2.17 tok/s        8.40 tok/s
after              5.15 tok/s       19.37 tok/s
```

Three runs each way. Before: 59.10, 59.09, 59.11 seconds. After: 24.88, 24.86, 24.88 seconds.

The same model in bf16 is not affected either way, 4.10 tok/s compiled against 4.04 eager, so this is specific to the int8 path.

No setting recovers it. `--enforce-eager` is the only mitigation and it still lands at 5.02 tok/s, below the patched number, and it turns off compilation for the rest of the model.

### The fix

Register `int8_scaled_mm_func` with a fake impl and call that from `apply_weights`. This mirrors what `w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm_func` already does a few lines below.

Output is unchanged. `torch.allclose` against the unpatched kernel passes at rtol 1e-2 atol 1e-2, and generation on the 27B model reads the same as before.

### Testing notes

I only have gfx1151, so that is the only hardware this was measured on. On CUDA the cutlass int8 kernel is normally picked ahead of the Triton one, so fewer users reach this path there and I could not measure it. The change is platform neutral. It adds a wrapper and does not touch the kernel or the tile selection.

This is int8 w8a8 only. AWQ, GPTQ and compressed-tensors W4A16 go through Marlin, `awq_triton` or `wNa16` and are untouched.

### Repro without a large model

```python
import torch
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.triton_scaled_mm import triton_scaled_mm

N, K = 34816, 5120
w = torch.randint(-127, 127, (K, N), dtype=torch.int8, device="cuda")
ws = torch.rand(N, 1, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
x = torch.randint(-127, 127, (1, K), dtype=torch.int8, device="cuda")
xs = torch.rand(1, 1, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")

c = torch.compile(triton_scaled_mm, dynamic=True, fullgraph=True)
c(x, w, xs, ws, torch.bfloat16, None)
```

Time the compiled call against the plain one. On gfx1151 the compiled one is about 29 times slower.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Remove the legacy Ray compiled-graph executor
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Remove the legacy Ray compiled-graph executor (`RayDistributedExecutor`). `RayExecutorV2` has been the default Ray backend; the legacy one was only reachable with `VLLM_USE_RAY_V2_EXECUTOR_BACKEND=0`.

## Claims

- `--distributed-executor-backend ray` always uses `RayExecutorV2`.
- Deletes `vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor.py`, `RayPPCommunicator`, and the V1-only `ray_utils` helpers (`RayWorkerWrapper`, the Ray `FutureWrapper`, `detach_zero_copy_from_model_runner_output`): −1257 / +14 lines.
- Removes the compiled-graph env vars `VLLM_USE_RAY_COMPILED_DAG_CHANNEL_TYPE`, `VLLM_USE_RAY_COMPILED_DAG_OVERLAP_COMM`, `VLLM_USE_RAY_WRAPPED_PP_COMM`.
- No behavior change for default configurations.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run` (ruff, mypy, forbidden imports, Buildkite checks): passed.
- Local run on 4x GB200 of `tests/utils_/test_ray_utils.py`, `tests/test_ray_env.py`, `tests/distributed/test_ray_v2_executor.py`: 28 passed. The 17 failures/errors in that run were all worker init failing with `Free memory on device cuda:0 (14.19/184.31 GiB) ... less than desired GPU memory utilization`, because another user's long-running vLLM processes occupy GPUs 0–1 on the shared node. A rerun of the 2-GPU cases on the free GPUs is in progress; I'll post results here.
- CI coverage: the existing `RayExecutorV2` Buildkite jobs (CUDA and MI355) run `test_ray_v2_executor.py`, `test_ray_v2_executor_e2e.py`, and the Ray cases of `test_pipeline_parallel.py` and `test_basic_correctness.py`. They already ran on V2 via `export VLLM_USE_RAY_V2_EXECUTOR_BACKEND=1`, which this PR drops because V2 is now unconditional.

## Details

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR removes the legacy Ray executor; searched open PRs for "ray executor", "RAY_V2_EXECUTOR", and "compiled DAG ray".

**Out-of-tree compatibility:** `vllm-project/tpu-inference` and `vllm-project/vllm-torchtpu` still read `envs.VLLM_USE_RAY_V2_EXECUTOR_BACKEND` on their Ray platform paths, so the env var stays defined for one release as a deprecated no-op (default `1`; removal planned for v0.34). Their own legacy executors import `vllm.v1.executor.ray_executor` and will break, but only when a user sets the flag to `0`. `_wait_until_pg_ready`, `WORKER_SPECIFIC_ENV_VARS`, and `RayExecutorV2`/`RayWorkerHandle`, which they also import, are unchanged. Setting `VLLM_USE_RAY_V2_EXECUTOR_BACKEND=0` against vLLM itself is now silently ignored.

**Follow-ups:** #61713 (stacked on this PR) removes `initialize_ray_cluster(require_gpu_on_driver)` and its driver-node pin, un-skips prompt embeds on Ray in `test_basic_correctness`, and corrects the `ray[cgraph]` requirement comment. The deprecated `VLLM_USE_RAY_V2_EXECUTOR_BACKEND` will be removed in v0.34.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][PCP] Align MoE routing padding with gathered tokens
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The non-all-to-all PCP path gathers hidden states and router logits across PCP ranks, but the router still reads the rank-local padding mask. With N local rows and P PCP ranks, routing processes P*N rows while the mask still has N entries. CUDA top-k checks that the mask length matches the token count and can raise an `is_padding` size mismatch.

This PR aligns the MoE padding mask with the PCP-gathered token rows and restores the original rank-local mask in a `finally` block. The dispatch/combine interfaces and PCP1/all-to-all paths remain unchanged. Regression tests cover PCP1/2/4, the all-to-all bypass, per-forward caching, and exception cleanup.

A search of open PRs covering PCP padding, PCP MoE, and the relevant padding-cache key found no equivalent fix. Nearby PRs #53639, #60049, and #56258 address different paths.

## Implementation

- Non-all-to-all PCP routing receives a padding mask with the same rank-major layout and row count as the gathered hidden states.
- The original local padding mask is restored on normal and exceptional exits.
- The gathered mask is cached per forward context and reused across MoE calls.

## Validation

### Environment

- Model: official `mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603` native FP8 checkpoint.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93`.
- Hardware: two nodes, each with 4x NVIDIA H20 GPUs.

### vLLM startup arguments

```bash
# Set MASTER_ADDR to the reachable IP address of the master node.
vllm serve /models/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 19180 \
  --served-model-name mistral-small4-pcp-ab \
  --config-format mistral \
  --load-format mistral \
  --tokenizer-mode mistral \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --master-addr "${MASTER_ADDR}" \
  --master-port 29511 \
  --language-model-only \
  --enforce-eager \
  --attention-backend TRITON_MLA \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --max-model-len 4096 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --block-size 64 \
  --kv-cache-dtype auto \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-async-scheduling
```

### Result

**Without this fix** (baseline): 
With the unmodified image and model, all seven native weight shards loaded (29.34 GiB per rank). The unpatched run then failed during vLLM's standard startup memory profiling, before the API server became ready:

```text
RuntimeError: .../topk_softmax_kernels.cu:785, is_padding size mismatch, expected: 4096
```

**With this PR**:
Applying the `_sequence_parallel_context` change from this PR at startup allowed the TP2/PCP2 deployment to start and generate successfully. It passed all five chat smoke requests, including a 2,235-token input and concurrent requests of different lengths.

Using the official `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` scoring logic, we evaluated all 1,319 test examples with 5-shot prompts, temperature=0, seed=42, `max_tokens=256`, and concurrency=4. Results:

| Run  | GSM8K | Invalid answers | Runtime result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Baseline + TP4/PCP1 | 1191/1319 (90.2957%) | 0 | Full evaluation completed; 0 API errors and 0 Pod restarts |
| Baseline + TP2/PCP2 | Could not run | — | Failed during startup profiling with the padding-size mismatch above |
| This PR applied + TP2/PCP2 | 1197/1319 (90.7506%) | 0 | Full evaluation completed; 0 API errors and 0 Pod restarts |

Removed:

commits.pr_title: [CI] Fix /ci run reporting a failed merge on fork PRs
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix a race in the `/ci run` auto-merge from #61592: on fork PRs the bot merged `main` successfully but then reported "could not merge (API returned 404: Not Found)" and started no CI.

## Claims

- `/ci run` no longer reports a failed merge (and skips CI) when the merge into a fork branch succeeded.

## Validation

```bash
cd .github/workflows/scripts
uv run --no-project --python 3.12 python -m unittest test_run_ci_command
# Ran 60 tests ... OK
```

New regression test `test_run_waits_for_fork_merge_commit_to_reach_base_repo` (first post-merge compare returns 404, next succeeds) fails on current `main` (no build created) and passes with this change. pre-commit passes.

## Details

**Seen on #61556:** `/ci run` at 17:46:35; the bot's merge commit `8bc708e` landed on `jinzhen-lin/vllm` at 17:46:57; the bot replied ❌ "...could not merge upstream `main` into this branch (API returned 404: Not Found)" at 17:47:02. A second `/ci run` started build #94876 on the same commit.

**Root cause:** after `update-branch`, the script polls the PR until its head SHA changes and then calls `compare/main...<new head>` on `vllm-project/vllm` to confirm the branch is fresh. For fork PRs the PR's head SHA updates before the new commit is reachable from the base repository (`refs/pull/N/head` syncs a few seconds later), so that compare returns 404, and every `ApiError` was treated as a failed merge.

**Fix:** treat a 404 from the post-merge compare as "not visible yet" and keep polling within the existing ~2 minute window. Other errors still fail. Waiting until the compare succeeds also makes sure the commit is reachable from the base repo before Buildkite checks it out.

## Overview

Fixes a Kimi-K3 startup crash on ROCm (`'MLAAttention' object has no attribute 'W_UK_T'`) that appears once #53123 turns AITER FP8 BMM off by default.

## Claims

- `KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper._fused_qk_prep_supported()` no longer reads `attn.W_UK_T` in `__init__`.
- The fused decode Q-prep path stays enabled when neither AITER BMM is on, instead of being silently disabled.

## Validation

- CI failure: MI355 LM Eval Spec Decode (Fixed-length FP8), `Kimi-K3-pruned75-DSpark-AITER-TP4`, [amd-ci #14622](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/14622#01a13ad1-6ae5-4cca-85f2-e72e6996548a).
- Called `_fused_qk_prep_supported` against an `nn.Module` fake MLA attention in that build's CI image (includes #53123):

| FP4 BMM | FP8 BMM | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| off | off | `AttributeError: W_UK_T` | True |
| off | on | False | False |
| on | off | True | True |

- Not run end to end locally: the 475 GB checkpoint doesn't fit on my box. CI's MI355 Spec Decode job covers it.

## Details

`_fused_qk_prep_supported()` runs in `__init__`, but `MLAAttention.W_UK_T` is only created in `process_weights_after_loading`. Before #53123, FP8 BMM was on by default, so the expression short-circuited and never read it. `process_weights_after_loading` always creates `W_UK_T` when FP4 and FP8 BMM are both off, so the check isn't needed. Using `getattr(..., None)` instead would have turned the fused path off for every such config. No open PR fixes this; #60110 edits `_fused_decode` but not this gate.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Parser] Stream Gemma4 string tool arguments incrementally
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Stream Gemma4 `<|"|>` string tool arguments incrementally and in linear time by adopting the `arg_value_extender` hook from #61253, and fix the engine so a live extender runs before the `arg_structural_chars` gate. Follow-up to #61253; same root cause as the DeepSeek symptom in #52846 / #58780.

## Claims

- Gemma4 string argument bodies now stream token by token. Before, a value without one of `,:{}[]<` arrived as a single fragment when its closing delimiter did.
- Long string arguments no longer cost quadratic parser time. A 32 KB code value drops from 7.0 s to 0.15 s of parser CPU on this machine; the converter runs a constant 8 times instead of 5008.
- Accumulated streamed arguments are byte-identical to the previous streaming path and to non-streaming extraction, including streams cut inside a value.
- Engine: a live extender now receives every delta. Before, the `arg_structural_chars` gate dropped non-structural deltas from the open value and the stream truncated at the next conversion. GLM, the only previous extender user, sets no gate and is unaffected. `ParserEngineConfig` rejects an extender without `arg_converter` or with `stream_arg_deltas=False`, which the engine silently ignored.

## Validation

Tests (CPU-only machine, no GPU; see Details for the eval gap):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine tests/tool_parsers/test_gemma4_tool_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_gemma4_reasoning_parser.py -q
# 6105 passed
```

New tests in `tests/parser/engine/test_gemma4_streaming_reasoning.py::TestGemma4ArgValueExtender` compare the extender against the converter-only engine (`arg_value_extender=None`) and against non-streaming extraction at chunk sizes 1, 3, 7 and 64, with and without a schema, over values containing commas, braces, parens, whitespace runs, every proper prefix of `<|"|>`, quotes, backslashes, unicode and lexer terminals (`call:`, `:`, `{`); truncated streams cut inside the value; the closing delimiter split at every offset; the factory's refusals (closed value, open key, nested value, duplicate key, bare value, partial opener); and that converter calls do not grow with value length. With the engine gate reorder reverted, 31 of these tests fail, which is the evidence that the engine change is load-bearing.

`tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py::TestArgValueExtender` pins the engine contract: the gate-order test fails on the previous engine, and the config validation test covers both rejected configurations.

Differential fuzz (not checked in): a grammar-based generator over Gemma4's format, random nesting, duplicate and delimited keys, both brace and paren call forms, with and without schema coercion, delivered as random char chunks, token-ID batches with `<|"|>` as its own token, and truncated streams with cut points biased to whitespace, closers and partial delimiters. 33,000 cases over three seeds, zero divergences in content, reasoning, tool names or accumulated arguments. Mutation check: breaking the extender's hold-back, escaping or split-delimiter window each made the fuzz fail in 12-23% of cases.

Benchmark (`parse_delta`, 4-char chunks, mock tokenizer, parser time only):

| Content | Chars | Extender | Parser time | Converter calls | Ticks emitting arguments |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| code | 2k | off / on | 36 ms / 10 ms | 319 / 8 | 284 / 503 |
| code | 8k | off / on | 459 ms / 38 ms | 1258 / 8 | 1129 / 2004 |
| code | 32k | off / on | 7005 ms / 152 ms | 5008 / 8 | 4504 / 8004 |
| prose | 32k | off / on | 28 ms / 87 ms | 8 / 8 | 4 / 8004 |

Pre-commit passes on all changed files.

## Details

**Root cause.** `_compute_arg_delta` returned early for any delta without an `arg_structural_chars` character, before consulting a live extender. Gemma4 sets that gate to `,:{}[]<`, so a body delta like `Paris` never reached the extender or the converter, and the whole value was emitted when the close arrived. Every delta that did pass the gate re-parsed the full argument text, which is quadratic in value length and is why code-like values, full of structural characters, were the worst case.

**Engine change.** The gate now applies only when no extender is live; a live extender sees every delta. The factory is called after each accepted conversion and decides whether the raw text ends in an open value, because the engine cannot tell from converted JSON (converters serialise an open raw value as a closed JSON string). The `arg_value_extender` comment documents this and the lexer invariant extenders rely on: a terminal is never split across deltas, except that a held partial terminal is flushed as text at end of stream or before a token-ID terminal. The `_safe_arg_prefix` docstring is corrected to say the flag describes the returned prefix.

**Gemma4 extender.** `_parse_gemma4_fields` reports the key of an unterminated trailing string so the factory can confirm it is also the last key in the parsed dict (a duplicate key would otherwise stream into the wrong slot). The hard part is that `_gemma4_arg_converter` hides a tail of the open value until more text arrives: `.strip()` removes trailing whitespace, one trailing `}` or excess `)` is dropped as the call-body closer, and `_strip_partial_delim` removes a partial `<|"|>`. The extender keeps exactly that tail unemitted and uses it as the window that detects a split close, so its output stays a prefix of every later conversion, including the final flush of a truncated stream. `_drop_call_closer` is shared with the converter so the two cannot drift. Unlike GLM's tags, `<|"|>` is not a lexer terminal, so the window is required rather than defensive.

**Tradeoffs.** Prose values now cost about three times the parser time because every token is emitted instead of one lump; absolute numbers stay small and linear (87 ms for 32 KB). `Gemma4Parser` accepts `parser_engine_config` as an override, matching `Glm47MoeParser`, so tests can swap the converter or extender.

**Limitations.** A duplicate top-level key whose first value already streamed cannot be extended; both the old and new paths stop at the same point. That is pre-existing behaviour in the area of #53739. No model eval was run: this machine has no GPU. The change alters only when argument fragments are emitted, and the tests pin the accumulated text to the non-streaming result; a reviewer with a Gemma4 checkpoint could confirm by streaming a long file-write tool call with and without the change and diffing the concatenated arguments.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR adds an extender to any parser (`gh pr list --search arg_value_extender` is empty). #58780 fixes the same symptom for DeepSeek by relaxing the gate in the engine, which keeps the quadratic cost; that engine hunk is superseded by the reorder here, and the DeepSeek extender can follow as its own PR.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the analysis, the implementation, the tests and this description. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

commits.pr_title: [Quantization] Support compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE with FP8 activations via Mxfp4MoEMethod
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Load compressed-tensors checkpoints with MXFP4 weights and dynamic FP8 activations (e.g. `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MXFP4-DSFP8`, `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-MXFP4xFP8_BLOCK`, `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-MXFP4xFP8_BLOCK`, DeepSeek-V4-Flash converted to CT) and run them with the FP8 activations the checkpoint declares. Alternative to #59376 (cc @kylesayrs).

**Depends on #61556.** Humming 0.1.16, which `main` pins today, rejects FP8 (GS128) activations with MXFP4 weights, so these checkpoints fail to load with `--moe-backend humming` until #61556 lands.

## Claims

- MoE experts: `CompressedTensorsW4A8Mxfp4MoEMethod(Mxfp4MoEMethod)` only handles the `*_weight_packed` checkpoint naming and the declared activation scheme. Backend selection, weight conversion, size round-up, monolithic kernels and EPLB are inherited from the native MXFP4 method.
- The checkpoint's FP8 activation key reaches the Humming MoE backend. Before, it was dropped and Humming ran BF16 activations (W4A16) unless `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` was set.
- Dense linears with MXFP4 weights and FP8 inputs (GLM-5.3's dense MLPs target `Linear`) use a new `CompressedTensorsW4A8Mxfp4` scheme that requests FP8 activations, instead of the W4A4 scheme requesting MXFP4 activations.
- `get_moe_method` looks up the expert scheme with the layer's `ckpt_*_proj_name`, and DeepSeek-V4 (NVIDIA) passes `ckpt_names=("w1", "w2", "w3")`, so name-based targets such as `re:.*experts\.\d+\.w\d+$` match.

## Validation

H200 (SM90), `--moe-backend humming`, checked by inspecting the loaded layers.

| Model | Config | Dense MXFP4 linear | MoE experts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MXFP4-DSFP8 (real weights) | TP1 | n/a (FP8 block) | Humming, FP8 GS128 (W4A16 before this PR's 2nd commit) |
| GLM-5.3-MXFP4xFP8_BLOCK (dummy weights, 5 layers) | TP1, TP2, TP2+EP | Humming, FP8 GS128 (FP8 per-token before) | Humming, FP8 GS128 (BF16 before) |

These runs used the v0.32.0 release branch with #61556, and `main` with #61556 applied. With `main` alone, the Humming 0.1.16 schema check rejects the combination. EP selects `HummingGroupedExperts` and TP selects `HummingIndexedExperts`. Greedy outputs match between TP2 and TP2+EP.

GSM8K, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 1x H200 (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --temperature 0 --max-tokens 1024`, 1319 questions, 5-shot):

| Checkpoint / activations | Accuracy |
|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` BF16 | 0.956 |
| MXFP4-DSFP8, MoE W4A16 (previous behavior) | 0.958 |
| MXFP4-DSFP8, MoE W4A8 (this PR) | 0.961 |

Tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k mxfp4 -v  # 4 passed (H200, main)
pre-commit run --files <changed files>  # incl. mypy
```

The original commit was also validated on B300 (SM103): a layer harness loading a real `RoutedExperts` with random MXFP4 weights was bitwise equal to native `Mxfp4Config` across the default, monolithic TRTLLM, unaligned-shape, `triton_unfused`, `marlin`, `deep_gemm`, `flashinfer_cutlass` and `flashinfer_trtllm` backends. Converted DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 generated the same token ids and logprobs as the original checkpoint on 8 prompts.

## Details

**Root cause of the BF16 fallback.** For `Mxfp4MoeBackend.HUMMING`, the MoE conversion built Humming's input schema only from `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` (`TODO: read input_quant_config from quant_config`), so an unset env meant BF16. With schema fallback enabled, Humming also demotes group-scaled FP8 to A16 (`prefer wna16 for groupwise weight or groupwise input`). Output still looked correct, so the slower path went unnoticed. `Mxfp4MoEMethod` now takes an optional `activation_key`. The HUMMING conversion uses it with fallback disabled, unless the env override is set. Other backends ignore the key.

**Performance.** At the GLM-5.x expert GEMM shapes (N/K 4096/6144 and 6144/2048, 32 experts, top-8; `benchmarks/bench_humming.py` at the #61556 Humming pin), W4A8 is 1.4-1.8x faster than W4A16 for M >= 256. End to end, the small Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 1x H200 is 3-8% slower with W4A8 than with W4A16 across prefill- and decode-heavy runs (hidden 2048, expert intermediate 512, so the per-layer activation quantization is not amortized). This PR follows the checkpoint's declared scheme. `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` still overrides it.

**Limitations**
- ROCm, XPU and CPU have no MXFP4 linear kernel for FP8 activations, so MXFP4 x FP8 dense layers keep the previous MXFP4-activation path there, with a warning. MI300 CI hit this; the linear test is CUDA-only.
- Blackwell: dense linears now use Humming FP8, which is slower than FlashInfer W4A4 on SM100 but matches the checkpoint. The MoE still picks its Blackwell backend without the activation key, so it uses MXFP8 or BF16 activations instead of `DEEPGEMM_MXFP4` (FP8 GS128 x MXFP4). Hooking that up is left for a follow-up issue.
- The AMD, XPU, CPU and V4.1 DeepSeek model variants still need the same `ckpt_names` one-liner; untested here.
- The rename breaks the pre-processed weight cache, so `supports_pre_processed_weights` is off for this method.
- Converting DeepSeek-V4-Flash with vllm-project/compressed-tensors#902 also emits `shared_experts.w\d+` targets, while vLLM names that layer `shared_experts.down_proj`; that needs a fix in the converter or model.

**Not a duplicate:** #59376 targets the same scheme with a different design; only one should merge. #58714 adds a separate CT -> `HummingMoEMethod` route for the same checkpoints; this PR covers that path through the native MXFP4 method. #56523 and #56306 migrate the W4A4 method to the oracle and do not touch this scheme.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Length-aware candidate block selection in the decode indexer
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1's decode indexer writes its logits into a `[rows, max_model_len]` buffer, a width that must stay static for CUDA graphs (1M with the default `max_model_len`). Each row only holds its own context, but `select_candidate_blocks` scored every block of the full width and then ran `torch.topk(2048)` over all of them. At 1M that costs about 850 us per decode step, whatever the actual context length. This PR makes candidate selection length-aware.

- **Score only valid blocks.** `_block_scores_kernel` now runs a fixed `(rows, 32)` grid that walks each row's tiles only up to the row's end, and it writes each row's valid block count.
- **DeepSelect instead of `torch.topk`.** On the DeepSelect path, the block count is passed as DeepSelect's per-row `end`. Short rows are padded with -1. Candidate order does not matter, because the sparse expansion sorts. The full-width `torch.topk` path stays as the fallback for no DeepSelect, non-contiguous output, `topk > 4096` and narrow logits, and its behaviour is unchanged.
- **NaN rows.** DeepSelect leaves NaN rows only partly written, which can happen during warmup or capture on an uninitialized KV cache. On the DeepSelect path, NaN blocks are pinned like the newest block, as `torch.topk` ranks NaN first. NaN rows therefore still get complete, in-range candidates.
- **bf16 decode logits.** The decode indexer now asks DeepGEMM for bf16 logits when the top-k backend is `deep_select` and DCP is off. This halves the bytes that the top-k and candidate passes read. The logits kernel still accumulates in fp32 and only rounds the output, which is byte-identical to `bf16(fp32 logits)`. The other top-k backends and the DCP merge still get fp32.
- **Footprint.** `candidate_blocks.py`, the decode call in `sparse_attn_indexer.py`, and a `logits_dtype` passthrough on `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` (default fp32). The DeepSelect availability check reuses `has_deep_select()`.

## Kernel microbenchmark

`select_candidate_blocks` alone, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode shapes: 384 rows (64 requests x 6 tokens), logits width 1,048,576 (default `max_model_len`, ratio-1 candidate-source layer), 2048 candidate blocks of 8. 1 x GB300, FlashInfer CUPTI timing with CUDA graph replay and cold L2, median. Logits are continuous random values; random FP4 inputs give heavily tied logits, which is pathological for radix selection and does not match the model.

| context (tokens) | main, fp32 logits (us) | this PR, fp32 logits (us) | this PR, bf16 logits (us) | speedup (bf16 vs main) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 131,072 | 847.8 | 77.0 | 42.9 | 19.8x |
| 176,000 | 861.2 | 116.8 | 62.2 | 13.8x |
| 400,000 | 884.0 | 205.9 | 119.9 | 7.4x |
| 1,048,576 | 939.0 | 408.2 | 254.9 | 3.7x |

main's cost is flat because it always scores and sorts the full width. This PR scales with the context and is still faster at the full 1M.

The dense indexer top-k reads the same logits, so the bf16 switch also speeds it up. DeepSelect top-512 at 131K context, ratio-2 layer (65K keys) / ratio-1 layer (131K keys): fp32 42.2 / 62.7 us, bf16 28.8 / 45.4 us. The logits kernel itself takes the same time with fp32 and bf16 output (93.0 vs 94.2 us, 180.6 vs 181.5 us).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py -q -k "candidate or sparse_topk_remap"
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py
```

Also checked locally, without adding tests:
- Against the previous implementation, on 384-row decode inputs (1M width, random ends, `row_repeat=6`, rows shorter than 2048 blocks, empty rows, ends past the width), prefill rows with starts, and the fallback path: the selected candidate sets are identical. The only exception is an exact score tie at the 2048th block, where either choice is valid.
- The fallback path forced on is identical to the previous implementation (fp32). With bf16 logits, the DeepSelect path and the fallback select the same blocks, compared by score so ties do not count.
- NaN rows (fully NaN, and partly NaN) on the DeepSelect path: every id is in range and unique, nothing stale is left, and the NaN blocks are selected.
- bf16 paged MQA logits are byte-identical to the fp32 output rounded to bf16.

## Test Result

On 1 x GB300: 6 passed (the four `test_candidate_kernels_preserve_packed_bounds_and_padding` cases, including `out[:, ::2]` at 32768 columns, `test_select_candidate_blocks_tolerates_empty_rows`, and `test_sparse_topk_remap_bounds_nan_rows`). Pre-commit (ruff, format, typos, mypy) passes.

## E2E decode (DEP4)

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (DP4 x TP1 + EP) on one GB300 node. `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41` with the MXFP4 indexer cache and sparse indexer logits, DeepGEMM mega MoE, `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend deep_select`, DSpark (5 tokens, synthetic acceptance), `max_num_seqs=64`, default `max_model_len` (1M), `DecodeBenchConnector`. 256 random-token requests with 125,000 input and 8,000 output tokens, all admitted at once. The nsys window opens about 40 s in, at a context of about 131K. GPU time is per decode step and GPU, averaged over all GPU-steps in the window. The E2E runs used a DSv4.1 development tree whose `candidate_blocks.py` and `sparse_attn_indexer.py` are identical to main's, with and without this patch; the unit tests ran on this branch.

| | base | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| indexer + candidate selection (us/step) | 1698 | 886 |
| `_block_scores_kernel` (us/step) | 208 | 26 |
| `torch.topk` kernels (`computeBlockDigitCounts`, `gatherTopK`, sort, ...) (us/step) | 619 | 0 |
| target forward GPU busy (ms/step) | 24.11 | 23.36 |
| median ITL (ms) | 26.52 | 25.65 |

A rerun with the final code gives the same 886 us.

## Accuracy

GSM8K with lm-eval 0.4.13 on this PR: 1319 problems, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, 1024-token cap, concurrency 32, one DEP4 `vllm serve` (MegaAttn, MXFP4 indexer cache with sparse logits, DeepGEMM mega MoE, `deep_select` top-k, so the decode indexer runs with bf16 logits and the new selection path). DSpark used 5 speculative tokens with standard rejection sampling and adaptive verification off. Acceptance comes from the `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters over the eval.

| | strict match | flexible extract | acceptance length, incl. bonus | per-position acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|---|

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Apply the JSON schema in Cohere Chat v2 response_format
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Every `/cohere/v2/chat` request with `response_format={"type": "json_object", "json_schema": {...}}` fails with a 400, because the schema never reaches structured outputs. This change passes the schema through the field's `schema` alias, as the Anthropic adapter already does.

## Claims

- A Cohere Chat v2 `json_schema` response format now constrains the output to the schema, for both streaming and non-streaming requests, instead of returning a 400.
- `json_object` without a schema and `text` behave as before.

## Validation

Unit tests (CPU):

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/cohere
```

The 219 conversion and protocol tests pass. The 9 server tests in `test_chat_v2.py` start `vllm serve`, so I ran them separately against a CPU build with `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct`, and all 9 pass. The new `test_json_schema_reaches_sampling_params` fails on `main` with the same `VLLMValidationError` that causes the server's 400, and passes with this change. The existing `test_json_schema` is unchanged and passes both on `main` and with this change.

Live A/B on CPU: `VLLM_ENABLE_COHERE_API=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` (revision `7ae55760`) with `--structured-outputs-config.backend xgrammar`, temperature 0. Both runs used the same CPU build of `main` (`0f112d1`); the second added this change. The schema requires `capital` (enum `["Vienna"]`) and `population_millions`, with `additionalProperties: false`.

| `response_format` | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `json_object` + `json_schema`, non-streaming | 400: "You must use one kind of structured outputs constraint but none are specified" | 200: `{"capital": "Vienna", "population_millions": 10.5}` |
| `json_object` + `json_schema`, streaming | 400, same error | 200, same JSON |
| `json_object` without a schema (control) | 200, JSON | unchanged |

Pre-commit passes on the changed files, including the mypy hooks for Python 3.10 to 3.13.

## Details

Root cause: `JsonSchemaResponseFormat.json_schema` is declared with `alias="schema"`, and `OpenAIBaseModel` allows extra fields. `JsonSchemaResponseFormat(json_schema=...)` therefore stores the schema as an extra attribute and leaves the field `None`. `structured_outputs_from_response_format` reads the field, so the request ends up with no structured-output constraint and fails validation. This has been the case since the Cohere Chat v2 endpoint was added in #47189.

The existing `test_json_schema` reads the schema back through `model_dump()`, which includes the extra attribute, so it passes on `main` too. I kept it as is and added a test that checks the schema reaches the sampling params, which is what the server uses.

Duplicate check: I searched PRs and issues for "cohere json_schema", "cohere response_format", "cohere structured output" and `JsonSchemaResponseFormat`, and found nothing related. The open Cohere PRs (#52437, #44659) change other code.

I used AI assistance (Claude) to find, fix and test this bug and to write this description.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DFlash] Capture context combine and anchor in the draft CUDA graph
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Capture the rest of the DFlash/DSpark context preparation in the draft's FULL CUDA graph, ahead of the query forward: combine the target's auxiliary hidden states, publish the LiLiCorr context anchor, then precompute the context K/V. #57632 captured only the last step; the first two still ran eagerly before every replay.

- The target's auxiliary states are staged into a fixed-address buffer before replay. The buffer is allocated at capture, only when the draft captures FULL graphs, so memory profiling accounts for it and an eager fallback does not hold it.
- LiLiCorr owns a fixed-address copy of the rejection counts its anchor reads; DFlash, DFlash2 and DSpark skip that copy.
- Context rows beyond the graph's capacity, and non-FULL paths, still run eagerly.
- The eager warmup before capture is preserved, including the Kimi-K3 cache-pointer refresh from #58814.

Applies to the shared DFlash, DFlash2, DSpark and LiLiCorr path. Open-PR searches for `dflash graph context`, `combine_hidden_states` and `57632 in:body` found no PR capturing this prologue; #50658 instead moves Kimi-K3 auxiliary projection before the SP all-gather.

## Test Plan

- E2E decode ITL: TP4 + DSpark serving benchmark, base vs PR vs base again on one node.
- Accuracy and acceptance: full GSM8K with DSpark on TP4 (PR) and DEP4 (base and PR).
- Microbenchmark of the context prologue alone.
- Unit tests, including a new CUDA graph test of the captured context step.

## Test Result

### E2E decode ITL (TP4, DSpark)

| Workload | Base | PR | Base (rerun) | PR vs base |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 in / 1024 out, c=1 | 5.66 | **5.55** | 5.91 | −2% / −6% |
| 8192 in / 1024 out, c=1 | 5.68 | **5.54** | 5.91 | −2% / −6% |
| 128 in / 1024 out, c=8 | 10.84 | 10.81 | 10.81 | no measurable difference |
| 128 in / 1024 out, c=64 | 26.61 | 26.59 | 26.62 | no measurable difference |

Median ITL p50 (ms) of 3 repeats. Every PR run at c=1 (5.53–5.59 ms) is below every base run (5.55–5.97 ms). Batch-1 decode is host-bound, and host CPU time varies more across runs than GPU time: the base's c=1 ITL moved by about 5% between its two runs, so the gain is quoted against each (−2% vs the run before the PR, −6% vs the run after). At c=8 and c=64 the step is GPU-bound and the host saving is not visible.

<details>
<summary>Setup</summary>

- 4× GB200, one node and one job: base (`8fb16ea5a6`) → PR (`ff8da0a4d8`) → base again, from the same source path and venv. The follow-up commits `9286fbea34` and `32836b7d4e` only move the staging allocation, restrict the rejection-count copy to LiLiCorr and simplify the test; they do not change the DSpark path measured here.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`), TP4 (no expert parallel), `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41`, fp8 KV cache, prefix caching off, FlashInfer autotune off, NUMA bind.
- DSpark with 5 speculative tokens and synthetic acceptance length 6.0, so every draft is accepted (100% from `/metrics` in every run).
- Random dataset with range ratio 0, `--ignore-eos`, 4× concurrency prompts (at least 8), unique seed per workload, concurrency and repeat. Each side is warmed up on every workload first; no timed run had runtime JIT warnings or new DeepGEMM cache entries. No probes or profilers.

```bash
vllm serve <model> --tensor-parallel-size 4 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 131072 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":6.0}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' --numa-bind --numa-bind-nodes 0 0 1 1

vllm bench serve --backend vllm --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --random-input-len <128|8192> --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --max-concurrency <1|8|64>
```

</details>

### Accuracy and acceptance (GSM8K, DSpark)

| Topology | Side | GSM8K strict | Acceptance length, incl. bonus | Per-position acceptance |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| TP4, fixed verification | PR | 93.03% | 3.449 | 0.794 / 0.649 / 0.459 / 0.335 / 0.213 |
| DEP4, MegaMoE, adaptive verification | base | 92.57% | 3.365 | 0.792 / 0.641 / 0.441 / 0.310 / 0.181 |
| DEP4, MegaMoE, adaptive verification | PR, run 1 | 92.34% | 3.367 | 0.792 / 0.642 / 0.440 / 0.310 / 0.183 |
| DEP4, MegaMoE, adaptive verification | PR, run 2 | 92.49% | 3.330 | 0.793 / 0.635 / 0.430 / 0.299 / 0.173 |

Full GSM8K (1319 problems, 5-shot completions, greedy, 1024 output tokens, concurrency 32, strict match), one pass per server, 0 request errors, acceptance from the engine's `/metrics` counters. PR is `ff8da0a4d8`; the follow-up commits do not change the DSpark path.

- DEP4: base (`8fb16ea5a6`) and PR on the same node and source path. Acceptance matches within 1% and the per-position curves overlap; GSM8K differs by at most 3/1319, inside run-to-run noise (two DEP4 baseline repeats in #57632 differed by 18/1319).
- TP4: PR side only. It matches #57632's TP4 reference (3.471 / 93.03%).

<details>
<summary>GSM8K server configuration</summary>

Same flags as #57632's GSM8K runs, plus FlashInfer autotune off:

```bash
vllm serve <model> --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  <TP4: --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}'> \
  <DEP4: --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe","enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}'> \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enable_adaptive_verification":<false on TP4, true on DEP4>}'
```

</details>

### Microbenchmark (context prologue only)

Single GB200, real MXFP8 `main_proj` weights (`15360 → 5120`) and RMSNorm, simulated BF16 auxiliary states from three target layers, 5 speculative tokens (6 context rows per request). CPU is submission wall time, median of three runs of 200 alternating samples; GPU is FlashInfer CUPTI with cold L2 on the captured prologue.

| requests | context rows | CPU before (µs) | CPU after (µs) | GPU before / after (µs) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6 | 392.6 | 48.8 | 34.4 / 36.3 |
| 8 | 48 | 396.1 | 49.9 | 46.8 / 49.5 |
| 32 | 192 | 386.7 | 49.4 | 51.2 / 52.7 |
| 128 | 768 | 327.4 | 48.3 | 88.6 / 89.9 |
| 256 | 1536 | 331.9 | 50.0 | 154.3 / 156.0 |
| 1, prefill | 8192 | 350.0 | 386.7 | 791.3 / 794.9 |

Decode saves 0.28–0.35 ms of CPU per step. A prefill pays ~37 µs more because the projection is split between the graph prefix and the eager tail. Context outputs matched exactly for three fresh inputs per shape; padded GEMM shapes need not be bitwise identical in general.

### Unit tests

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_profile.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py
```

commits.pr_title: [Dependency] Upgrade FlashInfer to 0.7.1
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Upgrade FlashInfer from `0.7.0.post1` to `0.7.1` for standard CUDA and Rubin builds. Explicitly select the CuTe DSL KDA prefill backend to avoid the inference-tensor crash observed in the B200 Kimi K3 CI job.

## Claims

- Update the shared `flashinfer-python` pin to `0.7.1`, retaining upstream's common `flashinfer download-kernels` installation flow for CUDA and Rubin.
- Keep KDA prefill on FlashInfer with inference mode enabled. No FlashInfer modifications, metadata copies, or test changes are required.

## Validation

On an allocated NVIDIA GB300 node with FlashInfer 0.7.1, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, and nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, using an isolated checkout and the existing environment:

- Reproduced all three original KDA failures before the fix; all three passed afterward (prefill correctness, near-collinear keys, and cross-stream breakable CUDA graph).
- `pytest -v tests/models/kimi_k3 --ignore=tests/models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py tests/kernels/attention/test_kimi_k3_mla_fused_epilogue.py` — **260 passed, 154 skipped**. This is the B200 Kimi K3 CI test selection, executed on GB300. Tests used the environment's `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files requirements/cuda.txt vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/kda.py` — passed after rebasing.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

GPU tests were run before the final rebase; the rebase did not change Kimi implementation or test files. B200 execution, full model accuracy evaluations, and standard/Rubin container builds have not been performed for this revision. The earlier MI250 EAGLE3 acceptance failure remains unresolved and should be reassessed in CI; it is not established to be an existing main failure.

## Details

FlashInfer's automatic small-BH prefill path caches packed sequence metadata using `cu_seqlens._version`. Inference tensors have no version counter, so this raises before kernel launch. Explicit `backend="cute-dsl"` avoids that path without changing PyTorch inference mode.

This bypasses the small-BH optimization. GB300 CUPTI microbenchmarks (BF16, D128, bounded gate, cold L2, eager GPU timing; median of three blocks of 20 samples) measured:

| Heads / tokens | FlashKDA (us) | FlashInfer auto (us) | Explicit CuTe DSL (us) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 12 / 128 | 45.7 | 31.3 | 23.6 |
| 12 / 2,048 | 118.6 | 71.5 | 80.4 |
| 12 / 8,192 | 355.4 | 214.1 | 270.1 |
| 96 / 8,192 | 863.7 | 459.5 | 459.1 |

Auto was measured with ordinary metadata tensors to avoid the crash. Explicit CuTe DSL was faster than FlashKDA for these cases, but 12–26% slower than working auto selection for the two longer H12 cases. These are microbenchmarks, not end-to-end serving measurements. Output and final-state correctness were checked before timing.

Rebased onto upstream main `838526c7e5`. Upstream removed separate cubin/JIT-cache pins in favor of `flashinfer download-kernels`; this PR preserves that change. Rubin continues to use the shared FlashInfer pin.

The initial duplicate-work search found no other open PR implementing this version upgrade; this updates the existing PR rather than opening a duplicate. No associated issue. AI assistance (Codex) was used for implementation, investigation, and validation.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Capture DCP FULL cudagraphs with KV context
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On MRV2, GQA models with DCP produce garbage under the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraph mode, including the Qwen3-235B `-tp 8 -dcp 2` example in `docs/serving/context_parallel_deployment.md`. This PR captures DCP FULL graphs with KV context, as V1 already does (`get_dcp_dummy_context_len`).

## Claims

- Fixes GQA + DCP + FULL cudagraphs on MRV2. Qwen3-235B at TP=8 DCP=2: needle retrieval 0/9 → 9/9.
- No regression for MLA + DCP (DeepSeek-V2-Lite).

## Validation

8x H100, `main` @ de8291e24f, default settings. Needle: 6-digit code at depths 0.1/0.5/0.9 of ~8k/~31k/~100k-token prompts, greedy. gsm8k: 5-shot, chat template.

| Model | Build | Needle | gsm8k flex / strict | KV tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, TP=8 DCP=2 | `main` | **0/9** | garbage | 1,851,136 |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, TP=8 DCP=2 | this PR | **9/9** | 91.66 / 80.74 | 1,846,080 |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8, TP=8 DCP=1 | this PR | 9/9 | 92.80 / 81.50 | 925,920 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B, TP=4 DCP=2 | `main` | **0/6** | | |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B, TP=4 DCP=2 | `main`, PIECEWISE | 6/6 | | |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B, TP=4 DCP=2 | this PR | 6/6 | | |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite (MLA), TP=4 DCP=4 | `main` | 6/6 | 53.83 | 8,634,624 |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite (MLA), TP=4 DCP=4 | this PR | 6/6 | 54.89 | 8,634,624 |

gsm8k stderr is ±0.7–1.1 (Qwen3) and ±1.4 (DeepSeek).

Zero-context batches (64 concurrent one-token prompts after a long request, FA3): first-token logprobs at DCP=2 match DCP=1 exactly (64/64).

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507-FP8 -tp 8 -dcp 2 --max-model-len 131072
pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py  # new test fails on main
```

## Details

**Root cause.** For DCP, the FlashAttention metadata builder skips context attention on the host when no request has context (`should_skip_dcp_context_attention`, #40996). MRV2 captures FULL graphs from a dummy batch with `seq_lens == query_lens`, so every FULL graph records the skip path and replays ignore the KV cache. Piecewise and eager rebuild metadata each step and are unaffected.

**Fix.** On FULL capture with `cp_size > 1`, give the dummy batch `cp_size * cp_interleave` tokens of context through the existing `set_dummy_context`. Applied on both FULL capture paths, normal and DBO. Capture-time only.

**Limitations.**
- The FA2 decode/prefill split (`should_split_fa2_dcp_context_attention`) is still decided at capture; unchanged by this PR.
- `set_dummy_context` clamps context to `max_model_len - max_query_len`, so a capture size within `cp_size * cp_interleave` of `max_model_len` still gets zero context.
- The DBO path is not tested end-to-end (needs DeepEP).

**Alternative.** Forcing `skip_dcp_context_attention=False` in the FlashAttention builder during capture. The runner-side fix matches V1 and is backend-agnostic.

No existing PR or issue covers this; nearest are #59951 and #54300 (different code paths).

## Overview

The MiniMax-M3 AITER indexer selector now rejects index-head counts AITER has no kernels for. At attention TP=1 (4 index heads per rank), the server now fails at load with a clear error instead of crashing on the first decode step.

## Claims

- `aiter_indexer_unsupported_reason` accepts only 1 or 2 index heads, the counts AITER builds its MSA score kernels for (`SPARSE_DECODE_TABLE`/`SPARSE_PREFILL_TABLE`, unchanged from the `v0.1.24.post1` pin through AITER main).
- A new regression test in `test_minimax_m3.py` fails without the fix and passes with it.

## Validation

MI355 (gfx950). At TP=1, `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` crashed before the fix at the first forward with `pa_sparse_block_score_decode: no build for num_idx_heads=4`. With the fix it refuses to start with a configuration error. `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py` passed 10/10 runs.

At TP=2 the same AITER kernels run before and after. I ran 5 interleaved runs per column, each with a fresh server, using `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` and the fp8 index cache. Values are mean ± sd.

| `vllm bench serve` (4096 in / 256 out, conc 16) | Before | After |

| Mean TPOT (ms) | 18.83 ± 0.73 | 18.53 ± 0.86 |

| gsm8k (5-shot, n=1319) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| strict-match | 0.8799 ± 0.0089 | 0.8708 ± 0.0089 |

The selector only rejected head counts above the 16 MFMA columns, so 4 heads got through and failed inside AITER's kernel dispatch. A rejected config falls back to the platform-neutral indexer, which turns this case into a load-time error. TP ≥ 2 still gives each rank 1 or 2 heads, so it keeps the AITER path. The test asks the selector instead of naming an architecture, so it keeps working as more CDNA targets are added. No open PR fixes this. commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix Model Runner V2 startup for the GPT-OSS-120B EAGLE3 [short-context](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/gpt-oss-120b-Eagle3-short-context) and [throughput](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/gpt-oss-120b-Eagle3-throughput) drafts, which set `use_aux_hidden_state=false`.

## Claims

- Single-state EAGLE3 drafts receive the target's final hidden state.
- EAGLE3's default auxiliary-state path and other speculative methods keep their existing behavior.

## Validation

CPU: 32 tests passed, including nine new configuration cases; pre-commit passed, including mypy. Tested on `2521446` plus this patch.

GPU: B200 x1 / TP1, GPT-OSS-120B MXFP4, vLLM `c19c263` plus this patch, CUDA 13, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. Context 131072, GMU 0.90, max sequences 8, prefix caching off.

| Draft | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Throughput, k=1 | V2 startup fails: 2880/8640 width mismatch | Generates in eager and non-eager modes; natural acceptance in both |
| Short-context, k=3 | Not run | Generates in eager and non-eager modes; natural acceptance in both |
| Long-context, k=3 (multi-state reference) | Generates | Generates; auxiliary capture retained |

Eight fixed math/coding prompts, greedy decoding, normal EOS, 128-token cap; batches 1 and 8, one warmup and three measured repeats each.

<details>
<summary>Timings and output comparisons</summary>

Multi-state reference, identical rendered prompts and input token IDs:

| Batch | Before tok/s | After tok/s | Change | Before / after repeat ranges |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | 547.840 | 537.452 | -1.90% | 544.820–549.704 / 535.911–538.325 |
| 8 | 1897.596 | 1900.161 | +0.14% | 1892.264–1906.589 / 1894.052–1906.894 |

Throughput is total output tokens divided by total wall time, including prefill and decode. Three repeats per case; before and after used separate GPU allocations. These measurements do not establish performance improvement or non-regression.

Some batch-8 outputs were not bit-identical. The unmodified baseline also varied across repeated runs, and the target-only/speculative differences started at near-tied token choices.

</details>

<details>
<summary>CPU test commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py -q

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/eagle/eagle3_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py
```

</details>

## Details

GPT-OSS-120B has [`hidden_size=2880`](https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-120b/blob/b5c939de8f754692c1647ca79fbf85e8c1e70f8a/config.json): 2880 elements per token's hidden-state vector. Three-state EAGLE3 concatenates three target-layer vectors to width `3 × 2880 = 8640`, then projects them to the draft's hidden size.

These two drafts instead consume only the final target hidden state and have no auxiliary-state projection. V2 still captures three states, and [`combine_hidden_states`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c19c263ac8ea3fd6e1d2d689f0e4e725855d89cf/vllm/model_executor/models/llama_eagle3.py#L397) passes the 8640-wide tensor through unchanged. Copying it into the draft's 2880-wide input buffer fails.

The fix honors the flag during runner initialization, so the existing proposer uses the final hidden state instead.

Related: [#40656](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40656) proposed this fix but is closed and unmerged. [#50170](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50170) addresses fallback warnings, not this configuration bug. No equivalent open PR was found.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MRV2] Skip empty draft-token resets on request admission
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
On GH200, short-input embedding inference at high concurrency is **CPU-bottlenecked by the EngineCore main thread**, with GPU SM utilization only **~9–18%**. Skip unnecessary per-request draft-buffer indexing and zeroing when Model Runner V2 has zero speculative steps, improving throughput by **~11–28%** in the measured workload while preserving the stale-slot reset from [#39833](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39833) for nonempty buffers. The improvement is largely due to reduced GIL contention.



## Claims
- Remove unnecessary PyTorch operations from request admission for pooling and ordinary non-speculative generation.
- Preserve draft-token clearing on slot reuse whenever the buffer has columns, including speculative decoding and diffusion models.
- The PyTorch operation releases the GIL, leading to the main thread being unnecessarily preempted by other threads that could do their work while the main thread waits for the GPU instead.
- Existing pinned GH200 embedding benchmarks report +10.6% request throughput for short inputs at concurrency 512 and +25.0–28.2% at concurrency 2048 for this guard alone.


## Validation
Checks run for this change:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py -v -rs
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py
git diff --check
```

With short inputs on GH200, throughput plateaus at roughly **5–6k requests/s (~85–100k tokens/s)** while the EngineCore main thread is CPU-saturated and GPU SM utilization remains **~9–18%**. For comparison, 1024-token inputs reach roughly **400k tokens/s** on the same server. These observations identify per-request work on the engine's main thread as the short-input throughput bottleneck.

| Concurrency | Stock throughput | With guard, pass 1 / pass 2 (estimated) | Gain, pass 1 / pass 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | ~4.66k req/s | ~5.15k / ~5.15k req/s | +10.6% / +10.6% |
| 2048 | ~5.57k req/s | ~6.96k / ~7.14k req/s | +25.0% / +28.2% |

Configuration: `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Embed-1B-BF16`, FP8 quantization, v0.31.0 aarch64 container, one GH200, MRV2 with synchronous scheduling, 16 API servers, and unique random short text inputs. Two reverse-order benchmark passes used six runs per configuration. Engine cores 4–5, API-server cores 8–39, and client cores 40–71 were pinned on GPU 0's NUMA node. Stock pinning-validation repeats spanned 4741–4965 req/s; per-patch raw variability is unavailable here.

Server flags:

```text
--max-num-batched-tokens 65536 --max-model-len 32768
--max-cudagraph-capture-size 32768
--api-server-count 16 --chat-template-content-format openai
```



## Details
`RequestState` allocates `draft_tokens` with shape `[max_num_reqs, num_speculative_steps]`. Admission previously evaluated `self.draft_tokens[req_idx].zero_()` even when the row had zero elements. The guard tests the configured width before indexing.

**Why such a large improvement:** The reason seems to be GIL contention. The pytorch op releases the GIL and then the main thread spends time waiting in pthread_cond_timedwait to reacquire it. If GIL is not released at that point, other threads will acquire it when the main thread waits for the GPU instead, leading to better overlapping GPU and CPU work.

**Why short inputs matter for embedding models:** semantic search commonly embeds a short question or a few keywords to retrieve much longer passages. Short-query embedding is therefore a core online serving workload, even when the indexed documents are long.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Warm up top-k/top-p and greedy rejection kernels for speculative decoding
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With speculative decoding, Model Runner V2 compiles sampling kernels in the first verification steps instead of at startup, so the first requests stall.

- **Commit 1:** register the native top-k/top-p warmups on CUDA when speculative decoding is configured. #58465 limited them to ROCm, but verification always masks top-k/top-p with these kernels, never with FlashInfer's fused sampler. Target-only CUDA engines are unchanged.
- **Commit 2:** when a rejection sampler exists, run the scheduler warmup a second time with greedy requests. All-greedy batches skip logits processing, so the rejection kernels see BF16 logits, a variant the warmup never compiled. Fixes #54455.

Not a duplicate: #56654 and #58465 removed CUDA sampler registration for its startup cost; this re-enables only what speculative decoding needs. #54630 (open) targets #54455 with mixed warmup configs, but on current main it calls `Sampler.add_request` with the signature from before #56497.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py tests/model_executor/test_jit_warmup*.py`, and pre-commit including mypy.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (5 speculative tokens), TP4 on one GB300, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. Main, commit 1 and this PR were started interleaved on one node with a fresh Triton cache per start (4 starts each; other caches warm). After `/health`, each server got one streaming request (top-p 0.9 or greedy), then 64 concurrent mixed requests. Compiles were counted with `--jit-monitor-verbose`.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 219 passed, 1 skipped on main and on this PR. pre-commit and mypy pass.

| | main | + commit 1 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| First top-p request, 2nd token | 2.07 / 2.09 s | 0.45 / 0.44 s | 0.43 / 0.45 s |
| First greedy request, 2nd token | 1.58 / 1.50 s | 1.47 / 1.62 s | 0.42 / 0.42 s |
| Compiles in the 64-request burst | 27 | 0–5 | 0 |
| Warmup time¹, cold Triton cache | 37.2 s | 52.9 s | 55.0 s (greedy pass 2.0 s) |
| Warmup time¹, warm Triton cache | 26.6 s | 26.1 s | 27.0 s (greedy pass 1.0 s) |

¹ JIT kernel warmup plus `warmup_kernels`. Commit 1 adds 22.1 s of registry warmup (120 more keys) and saves 6.5 s in `warmup_kernels`, which on main compiled these kernels itself.

TTFT doesn't change (0.40–0.57 s on all builds); the first token comes from prefill. The stall was in the first verification step, before the 2nd token. Greedy outputs are byte-identical across the three builds, and acceptance length is unchanged (2.84).

Limits: target-only batches that can't use the fused sampler still compile on first use, as on main. Seeded requests (#54425) aren't covered. Only tested on GB300 with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark; ROCm and pipeline parallelism are untested.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Don't crash DeepGEMM MegaMoE warmup when get_bf16_mega_gate_config is missing
commits.pr_body:
**Before:** A server started with `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe` on a model whose MoE layers use the bf16 mega gate crashes during kernel warmup with `AttributeError: module 'deep_gemm' has no attribute 'get_bf16_mega_gate_config'`.

**After:** Warmup completes. When DeepGEMM does not export `get_bf16_mega_gate_config`, the MegaMoE warmup buckets M values by `block_m` only.

## Overview

#60468 made `_get_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_m_values` call `dg.get_bf16_mega_gate_config` to pick one warmup M per gate config. #61149 moved the DeepGEMM pin to `6ce1c5ec`, which no longer exports that op. Every MegaMoE warmup that uses the mega gate now fails:

```
kernel_warmup.py:244 -> deep_gemm_warmup.py:511 -> :504 -> :366
AttributeError: ... has no attribute 'get_bf16_mega_gate_config'
```

This PR checks `hasattr(dg, "get_bf16_mega_gate_config")` and uses an empty gate config when the op is missing.

## Claims

- MegaMoE warmup no longer crashes when the installed DeepGEMM lacks `get_bf16_mega_gate_config`.
- Behavior is unchanged when the op is present.

## Validation

Existing unit tests:

```
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .
pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py
# 8 passed
```

Real module, with the vendored DeepGEMM from the precompiled wheel (`vllm.third_party.deep_gemm`): `hasattr(dg, "get_bf16_mega_gate_config")` is `False`, and `_get_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_m_values` (EP=4, 256 experts, top-k 6, 8192 tokens, mega gate on) now returns `[106, 256, 602, 2565, 7901, 8192]` instead of raising.

End to end on 4x B300: a DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint with `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192` finishes DeepGEMM warmup (1254/1254), passes `/health`, and answers a completion request ("The capital of France is" -> " Paris.").

No open PR fixes this: searching open PRs for `get_bf16_mega_gate_config` finds none, and #61538, which edits the same function, keeps the call.

## Details

Coverage trade-off: without gate configs, warmup no longer picks one M per distinct bf16 mega gate config. Gate configs that do not line up with a `block_m` bucket are not warmed and will JIT on the first request that hits them. This costs first-request latency, not correctness.

## Follow-up

A follow-up PR will reintroduce `get_bf16_mega_gate_config` in vllm-project/DeepGEMM and bump the vLLM pin, which restores full warmup coverage for the mega gate. This guard can stay afterwards so a mismatched external `deep_gemm` install does not crash the server.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix][MLA] Fix FP8 MLA prefill unpad for interleave-padded heads
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
The gfx950 FP8 asm MLA prefill pads heads to a multiple of 16. When the target is a multiple of the real head count (8 → 16, e.g. Kimi-K2.x at TP8), `get_mla_padded_q` uses `repeat_interleave`, but the output was sliced back as `[:, :num_heads]`, which is only correct for tile padding. The model then attends with the wrong heads and produces garbage. Introduced by #51040.

## Claims
- Restores accuracy for interleave-padded head counts: Kimi-K2.6 MXFP4 TP8 GSM8K 0.027 → 0.933.
- No performance change: same kernels; the unpad copy is still one kernel at the same cost.
- Adds the 8-head (interleaved) case to `test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_prefill.py`.

## Validation
Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4, TP8, MI355X, fp8 KV cache. GSM8K 5-shot, `lm_eval --model local-completions ... --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`, num_concurrent=64:

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| Before (upstream main) | 0.0273 ± 0.0045 | 0.0235 ± 0.0042 |
| After (this PR) | 0.9333 ± 0.0069 | 0.9333 ± 0.0069 |

Torch profiler, random 1024/1024, 64 prompts, concurrency 64: 40 kernels per prefill MoE layer before and after.

Unit test on MI355X: `pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_prefill.py`

| Code under test | Result |
|---|---|
| This PR | 12 passed |
| Upstream unpad, with the new test cases | 2 failed, 10 passed: only `test_fp8_prefill_matches_reference[128-8]` and `[512-8]` fail |

<details>
<summary>Failure details on the upstream unpad</summary>

- `[128-8]`: mismatched elements 81,670 / 131,072 (62.3%), greatest absolute difference 4.5 (atol 0.1)
- `[512-8]`: mismatched elements 230,240 / 524,288 (43.9%), greatest absolute difference 4.5 (atol 0.1)
- All tile-padded (12, 24) and unpadded (16) cases pass on both versions.
</details>

## Details
Real heads sit at stride `nhead // num_heads` after `repeat_interleave` and at `[0:num_heads]` after tiling; the fix selects accordingly. Existing test head counts (12, 16, 24) only exercised tile padding.
No duplicate: no open issue or PR addresses this; #59966 changes `get_mla_padded_q` but keeps `repeat_interleave` for the divisor case.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Nemotron-Parse] Do image rescale/normalize on the device
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Opts `NemotronParseForConditionalGeneration` into vLLM's existing `mm_device_do_normalize` path, so the fixed 2048x1664 canvas travels to the device as `uint8` and the rescale/normalize happens in `FusedMMInputNorm` instead of as single-threaded CPU work inside the engine process.

Please do aware this change depends on pending tied embedding fix for nemoparse2.0 embedding.

The checkpoint ships its image processor as remote code, and its `preprocess(self, images, return_tensors=None, **kwargs)` **ignores** the `do_rescale` / `do_normalize` kwargs that `MultiModalConfig.merge_mm_processor_kwargs` injects when the feature is on: it always runs `ToTensor` and normalizes from `self.do_normalize`. Setting the model flag alone would therefore normalize twice. The `_call_hf_processor` override replays the processor's own pipeline up to (but not including) `ToTensor` to produce the raw canvas, and raises -- pointing at `--no-mm-device-do-normalize` -- if a checkpoint does not expose that pipeline, so "feature on => `uint8`" holds by construction.

## Claims

- `supports_mm_device_do_normalize = True`; `build_mm_input_norm()` builds the norm and `_process_image_input` applies it unconditionally, as in the other models that opt in. With the feature off that is `IdentityInputNorm`, i.e. a plain cast.
- With the feature off, behaviour is identical to today.
- Both published checkpoints are handled: v1.2 (albumentations `transform` branch) and 2.0 (`_pad_to_size` branch).
- Payload per request drops 40.89 MB fp32 -> 10.22 MB uint8.

## Validation

Run on the latest `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` = `0.31.1rc1.dev23+g43b4aaea3`, whose `nemotron_parse.py` is byte-identical to this patch's parent and whose `layers/fusion/mm_input_norm.py` is byte-identical to this branch -- so the Triton `forward_cuda`, `IdentityInputNorm` and `_load_norm_params` exercised here are the ones this change targets. One H100, `--dtype bfloat16 --trust-remote-code --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.25 --max-num-seqs 16`.

Greedy request on a sample document page (`max_tokens 512, temperature 0, top_k 1, repetition_penalty 1.1, skip_special_tokens false`):

| engine | flag | dtype at model | `input_norm` | output sha256[:16] | tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| patched | on | `uint8` | `FusedMMInputNorm` | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |
| patched | off | `bfloat16` | `IdentityInputNorm` | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |
| unpatched | off | `bfloat16` | - | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |
| unpatched | on | `bfloat16` | - | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |

Unpatched + on logs `Model does not support mm_device_do_normalize, forcing ... False`, confirming the flag is the only opt-in.

**Numerics** -- device path vs the host path it replaces:

| case | bf16 | fp16 | fp32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| real page, 10,223,616 elements | **equal, 0 mismatched** | equal, 0 | max abs 2.4e-07 |
| all 3x256 possible byte values | **equal, 0 mismatched** | 3 at 1 ULP | max abs 4.8e-07 |
| `forward_cuda` vs `forward_native` | equal, 0 | equal, 0 | max abs 1.2e-07 |



**Latency**, 3 interleaved reps per arm, fresh server each, identical flags:

| | encoder-only p50 (`max_tokens=1`) | c=1 p50 | c=8 aggregate |
|---|---|---|---|
| on | **132.5 ms** | **131.8 ms** | 937.9 tok/s |
| off | 263.1 ms | 261.5 ms | 772.7 tok/s |

**1.99x**, with the per-rep ranges non-overlapping across all six reps, and +21% aggregate throughput at c=8. 

The win is, An isolated single-threaded CPU microbenchmark attributes the win: the processor's float work goes 160.3 ms -> 5.9 ms.

The added `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_nemotron_parse.py` passes (2 passed).

Re-verified after making `input_norm` unconditional, same nightly, one H100: both flag arms produce identical output (`b37da04a78014080`, 5 greedy reps each), TTFT p50 226.8 -> 118.6 ms. With the feature off the unconditional call is bit-identical to the `pixel_values.to(dtype)` it replaces -- 0 differing elements of 10,223,616, in bf16, fp16 and fp32 -- so the default path is unchanged. Deleting `_resize_with_aspect_ratio` or `_pad_to_size` from the processor raises a `RuntimeError` naming `--no-mm-device-do-normalize`.

## Details

`_build_uint8_canvas` depends on three attributes of the checkpoint's remote-code image processor: `_resize_with_aspect_ratio`, `_pad_to_size` and `transform`. Two are private by convention and none is a stable API. If they change, the lookup raises and the error names `--no-mm-device-do-normalize`, so the failure is loud instead of a silent loss of the speedup. The cleaner fix lives in the checkpoint: `preprocess` should honour its own `do_rescale` / `do_normalize` kwargs, after which this override can be deleted entirely. I am happy to drop the override and gate the feature on that instead if reviewers prefer.

Reproducing the `b37da04a78014080` output on `NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0` additionally requires the tied-`lm_head` fix (#60272, a re-land of #53020); without it that checkpoint's output head is randomly initialized and the server emits garbage while reporting healthy. That fix is independent of this change and was applied only for the validation runs above.

Not covered: CUDA only (`forward_xpu` / `forward_oot` are untouched and untested); one image per request, which is this model's `get_supported_mm_limits`.

commits.pr_title: [Benchmark] Add vllm bench forward: exact-shape forward timing
commits.pr_body:
> Commits: *[Benchmark] Add vllm bench forward*, the *model-microbenchmark* agent skill, and *Support DCP*. No changes to the model runner or model code.

## Overview

Add `vllm bench forward`: time the model forward of an **exact** batch (prefill, chunked prefill, prefix hit, decode, spec-decode verify, or any mix), built without the scheduler and run through the real `execute_model`, captured as a one-shot CUDA graph. Works single-GPU and with DP/TP/EP/DCP across nodes via `torchrun`.

```bash
vllm bench forward --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --case decode=64*1@8192 --case prefill=8192 --case mix=4096,32*1@8192
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \
  --model ... -dp 4 --enable-expert-parallel --shapes shapes.json
```

## Claims

- Exact shapes: requests are `[N*]Q[@K][c][:D]` (query length, KV length including the query, draft tokens). A prefill's prefix is a prefix-cache hit (SWA bounded replay on DeepSeek-V4.1) unless `c` marks a chunked prefill. Every run checks that the runner built exactly that batch.
- Accurate GPU time: one-shot FULL graph even for prefill (host-side plans are correct by construction, since the graph only replays the batch it captured). Rendezvous and timing events live inside the graph, so rank skew and launch gaps are excluded; each replay is reduced with MAX over ranks; per-replay jitter is reported (sample spread) and flagged above 0.5%.
- Realistic defaults for dummy weights: KV lengths vary +-50% (same on every DP rank, `--kv-len-jitter`); MoE routing is balanced per EP rank (`--routing auto`), replacing the degenerate routing of dummy gates.
- Matches independent references (below).

## Validation

GB200. CLI and unit tests (Benchmarks CLI job runs `tests/benchmarks/`):

```
pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py   # 3 passed
```

| batch | harness | bench forward |
| --- | --- | --- |

Also run: DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 DEP4 (1 node) and DEP8 (2 nodes, MNNVL), TEP4, prefix hits, verify. Median run-to-run reproducibility within ~0.3%; sample spread mostly 0.01-0.4% (higher on V4.1 DEP prefill, from MegaMoE cross-rank sync and host engram reads).

## Details

- **Flow per case:** build `SchedulerOutput` (disjoint block IDs across KV groups) -> zero the case's KV blocks -> `execute_model` twice: eager warmup (JIT, autotune), then capture/validate/time. For those two steps the bench shadows `runner.prepare_inputs` (to check the batch the runner built) and `model.forward` (to take over the eager model call) with instance attributes, then deletes them; the runner itself is unchanged. Requests are re-added on the second call; `sample_tokens` is never called, so the pending step state is dropped.
- **State restore:** the KV blocks a step writes are snapshotted and restored inside the graph before each replay, so in-place state (e.g. DeepSeek-V4.1's compressor) is identical across replays.
- **KV init:** zeros only for now (`--kv-init zeros`). Random KV was measured within 3% on DeepSeek-V4.1 at ~100K context, so its per-layout model code isn't worth it yet.
- **Routing:** forward hooks on `GateLinear` replace gate logits with a balanced fixture; this covers backends that route from logits, including monolithic FlashInfer TRTLLM (verified on Kimi-K3) and modular (verified on DeepSeek-V4: router top-k equals the fixture). Models that compute top-k themselves (e.g. MegaMoE's fused gate on DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 and Kimi-K3) instead get the fixture's `topk_ids` through a forward pre-hook on any experts module whose `forward` takes `topk_ids`; on DeepSeek-V4.1 DEP4 this matches the earlier model-local override within run-to-run noise (+0.05% to +0.8%). Grouped top-k is rejected; layers the fixture can't reach fail loudly.
- **Model code:** none.
- **Dependencies / limitations:**
  - Dummy-loaded DeepSeek-V4.1 loses MegaMoE shared-expert fusion (fixed by #60096); the bench's dummy loader finalizes early as a temporary workaround (TODO to remove).
  - Data-dependent kernels need realistic activations: #61323 keeps dummy norms neutral (e.g. V4.1 sparse top-k 27.8 ms -> 10.7 ms, real weights 10.6 ms).
  - The batch builder mirrors scheduler semantics (block counts, prefix-hit replay); the unit test and the per-run layout check guard against drift.
  - Model branches on `is_current_stream_capturing()` (e.g. DeepSeek-V4 short-context top-k, V4.1 mHC overlap) make small batches' graph output differ slightly from eager; reported, not asserted.
- **Agent skill:** `.agents/skills/model-microbenchmark` documents usage and pitfalls (dummy-weight artifacts, torch.compile models, timing spread) for agents.
